title: Roll-up readonly drop follow-ups from #35089: stdio MCP bridge droppedFields, changeset door list, readonly-flow lint and security.mdx
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzfr1xZSFZzCR8HnqXX

Follow-up of #34672 (insert half, PR #35089, merged as `cc5472eb85`; update half, PR #34752). These are the three nits from the seat's narrowing L2 6967339515 at `b2f55b4e`. They have a user-visible effect and were not folded before landing. Each one predates or sits outside the merged diff.

## N1 — stdio MCP bridge does not report `droppedFields`

The changeset's migration line and `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` say an MCP create reports the drop in `droppedFields`. The stdio bridge (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `create`) calls `engine.insert` with no `onFieldsDropped` and answers `{ ...data, ...written }`. So on that transport the caller is not told about the drop. Where the write result omits the key, the answer can echo the caller's value. That happens for a `min` / `max` / `avg` roll-up on a driver that returns the row it was handed. This predates #35089, and it is the same for every `readonly` column and for the update half. #35089 makes it more common.

Fix: pass `onFieldsDropped` in the bridge and answer `droppedFields` as the HTTP transport does. Alternatively, narrow the prose to "on the HTTP transport".

## N2 — changeset door list misses two narrowed doors

The insert-half changeset's door list leaves out two doors that are narrowed along with the rest:

- the public form submit (`packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts`). It is anonymous and the answer is the id only, so the submitter is not shown the drop.
- a caller's `overrides` on clone (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-data-crud.ts`), which reports the drop through the same listener as a create.

Both end in the engine's insert. This is a prose-only fix, made in a changeset or docs follow-up before the release that ships #35089.

## N3 — readonly-flow lint and `security.mdx` do not know the implicit roll-up lock

`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` only knows a declared `readonly: true`. So a user-run flow whose `create_record` or `update_record` sets a roll-up gets no lint finding, even though the engine now drops the value on both verbs. The static `readonly` section of `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx` does not name the implicit roll-up lock either. Both gaps date from the update half.

## Done when

- The bridge reports the drop (or the prose is narrowed), with a pin.
- The changeset or docs name both doors.
- The lint rule treats a `Field.summary` roll-up as readonly for flow writes, with a pin, and `security.mdx` names the lock.
